name: GUYANA

flag.title: Golden Arrowhead
flag.note: Green field; gold arrow edged black, tip red

lead: Guyana is on South America's north coast, but it feels Caribbean. English is the official language. Most people live by the sea. Behind them lie rainforest, flat-topped mountains and grassland. Oil was found in 2015, and the economy now grows very fast.

facts.label: Capital
facts.sub: Built below sea level on sea walls

facts.label: Land area
facts.sub: Roughly the size of the UK

geo: Guyana means 'land of many waters' in Arawak. More than 40 rivers cross it. The coast is below sea level, so Dutch-built sea walls hold back the ocean. Rainforest covers 80% of the land.
In the south is the Rupununi Savannah, a huge grassland. Flat-topped mountains called tepuis rise above it. Mount Roraima (2,772 m) inspired Conan Doyle's book The Lost World.
animals: Iwokrama Forest is a top place to spot a wild jaguar. Harpy eagles nest in the tallest trees. Giant river otters grow up to 1.8 m long.
The golden rocket frog lives near Kaieteur Falls and nowhere else. It raises tadpoles in giant bromeliad plants. Arapaima fish grow over 2 m long and breathe air.
culture: Guyana blends African, Indian, Amerindian and European roots. Cricket is a national passion. The national dish is pepperpot, a dark stew cooked for Christmas.
Diwali, Eid and Phagwah (Holi) are all public holidays. Each February, Mashramani carnival fills Georgetown with steel-pan music and big floats.
history: Dutch settlers built sugar plantations in the 1600s. They brought enslaved Africans to work them. Britain took over in 1814. After slavery ended in 1833, it brought workers from India.
Guyana became independent on 26 May 1966. In 2015 ExxonMobil found huge oil fields under the deep sea. By 2024 the economy was growing 43% a year.
wows: Kaieteur Falls is 4.5× taller than Niagara.
Georgetown sits below sea level, behind Dutch sea walls.
The golden rocket frog lives only near Kaieteur Falls.
On Roraima's top, clouds form below you.
Guyana is the only English-speaking country on mainland South America.
The arapaima fish breathes air, like a whale.

myths.fact: Piranhas mostly eat fish, insects and seeds. Bites on people are rare and small.

myths.myth: A black panther is its own kind of cat
myths.fact: It is a jaguar or leopard with dark fur. Its spots still show in sunlight.
